title: Tilda's Pebble Plan
markdown:
Tilda was a little rabbit who loved things neat and tidy. Her cozy home under the ground was perfect, with smooth grey pebbles lined up just so.

School was held under a friendly oak tree, where Mr Pine kept a kindly eye on the meadow class and never once asked a pebble to hurry. Tilda had a little worry. Her friend Wes the duck loved to share his loud ideas, and Tilda could not always share her own. It felt wobbly and messy.

One day, after Wes’s big talk about worms, Tilda’s nose twitched. Her fluffy ears drooped. Worry tickled her whiskers. “Oh dear,” she sighed. “How can we share ideas kindly without such a fuss?” She wished her thoughts were as neat as her pebbles.

Because she worried, Tilda had a new idea. “I shall collect polite phrases,” she told her reflection. Her determined face smiled back. She lined three extra pebbles on the windowsill, as if they were already taking turns.

The very next day at school, Wes was shouting about his plan for a super-splishy-splashy puddle. “It will be the best puddle ever,” he quacked. All the other creatures nodded, but Tilda’s ears twitched. She had an idea for a leaf slide, but Wes’s quacks were like a noisy waterfall.

Mr Pine, who taught under the oak because it was the finest classroom in the meadow, raised a patient paw. “One voice at a time,” he murmured, not unkindly.

“Excuse me, Wes?” Tilda said, her voice small but clear.

Wes paused. “Yes, Tilda?” he asked, softer now.

“I have an idea for a slide,” Tilda whispered, feeling a wobble. She held up a smooth grey pebble. “This pebble is for being quiet for a moment.”

Wes looked at the pebble, then at Tilda. “Oh,” he said. “A slide? That sounds wonderful.”

He took a deep breath. Instead of quacking, he said, “Tilda, tell us about your slide idea.”

Tilda beamed. She explained her leafy slide. Wes listened. Mr Pine nodded, as if a pebble had just taught the whole oak a useful trick.

“That’s a brilliant idea, Tilda,” Wes quacked, a happy happy quack.

They made the best splishy-splashy puddle with a super-duper leafy slide. Tilda’s pebble sat at the edge, waiting for the next turn. Everyone giggled with delight, and the meadow seemed even brighter with all their happy shared ideas.
characters: Tilda (a tidy pebble-loving rabbit), Wes (a loud-idea duck), Mr. Pine (an oak-tree school teacher)
author: StoryGen Community
